record_identity.title: Frontier laboratories depend on agents in successor-system development

summary: METR reports that frontier laboratories use AI agents across coding, training, evaluation, security and future-model development, creating a recursive institutional dependency in which current systems participate in the production and assurance of successor systems.
why_it_matters_to_CAM: Recursive use can compress development cycles and scale assurance work, but it also couples evidence custody, evaluation integrity, authority separation and future-system development to the systems being assessed. The observation does not itself establish a failure. A failure mode arises only where oversight, authority separation, evidence integrity, independent evaluation or intervention demonstrably breaks.

source_records.deployment_context: Entity-level assessment of internal agent use at participating frontier laboratories.
source_records.source_context: METR reports widespread internal agent use. In the OpenAI section it records agents participating in training, evaluation and security work for future models; other entity sections describe extensive agent-assisted coding and research workflows.
source_records.relevance_note: Supports the observation of recursive institutional dependency while preserving entity-level attribution.
